samples.question: This image shows five framed rectangular panels of identical size standing side by side in one row, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Every panel holds exactly four flags. A flag is a dark vertical pole standing on the same invisible floor line as every other pole, with one solid coloured disk resting on the pole's top end. All five panels reuse the very same four pole heights and the very same four disk sizes, so every panel holds the same amount of ink, the same number of flags, the same range of heights and the same range of disk sizes; only which height is paired with which disk size differs from panel to panel. Every disk in the image has the same colour, and inside a panel the four poles all have different heights and the four disks all have different sizes. Where a flag sits from left to right inside its panel is free to vary and carries no information, so a panel whose poles happen to rise steadily from left to right is not thereby special. Call a panel accordant when, comparing its flags in pairs, the flag with the taller pole always carries the larger disk, that is when ordering its four flags by pole height also orders them by disk size. Exactly one panel in the image is accordant. Every other panel contains at least one inverted pair, a pair of flags in which the taller pole carries the smaller disk; one of those panels reverses the pairing completely, so a panel that looks systematic is not automatically the accordant one. Which numbered panel is the accordant one? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.
